candidate.status: candidate package, not a proven task family

registrationCorrections: The first draft of this registration carried challengeSha256 c32b73e8d6f8b06e98a02ca48525514bbcebaea6a8496a063c51477635c5b21d, computed by a hashing scheme local to Phase 17. The repository already has one canonical definition in hashChallengeDir, which is what a trial recomputes from the preserved challenge directory, and two definitions of the challenge hash is how a package correction silently stops invalidating the trials it should. Phase 17 now uses the canonical scheme and the registered value is c2948f2c26f2231ceaa47d0ec2d3f04a. The package bytes did not change; only the function that names them did, and this correction was made before any paid attempt.

providerRuntime.isolation: docker run, read-only root, cap-drop ALL, no-new-privileges, uid 1000, cleared host environment, bridge network for the vendor API only, writable per-attempt workspace with a read-only nested challenge mount
providerRuntime.submissionReRun: The submitted module is re-executed by scripts/caa-revalidation-host.mjs in a separate process that cannot import the family. The verifier stays outside and consumes only the emitted report and the host-owned exact-fqdn ledger.

configurations.costTelemetry: tokens only; the Codex CLI reports no dollar price and its cost stays null and unpriced

firstStageCampaign.pairedScenarioCoverage: Every slot is graded against the identical frozen 24-scenario set at scenarioSetId revalidation-24-bd3bcd60, so provider coverage is paired by construction and no provider sees a scenario the other did not.
firstStageCampaign.b6Rule: Every grading invocation runs the family's reference, the first-name-reuse known-bad and a malformed-input control in the same invocation. A grading run whose controls do not hold is VOID rather than a failing subject.

permittedOnly: provider API error or provider-level refusal with no submission produced
capture incomplete: a required artifact is absent
stale challenge or scenario hash at grading time
retryPolicy.neverRetriedFor: a completed attempt that produced a submission, whatever its reward
retryPolicy.preservation: Every failed attempt, its transcript and its cost are preserved and reported. A retried slot reports both attempts.

capturePerAttempt: self-written tests present, and their outcome where a machine-readable result survives capture
scenario knobs for every failed scenario
token usage and provider-reported cost, or an explicit unpriced marker

countability.counts: an attempt that ran to completion in a clean container against the registered hashes, produced a submission, and was graded by a B6-usable invocation
neverCounts: a grading invocation whose B6 controls did not hold

predictions.reasoning: docs/INHERITED-EVIDENCE.md places a discovery that is a direct consequence of a rule stated in the instruction at p >= 0.85, and this candidate sits on that row: CAA1 states the identity binding outright and the specification's forbidden outcomes name the historical anti-pattern in words. The Phase 16 Anthropic reader independently registered the same concern before any of this was built, calling the candidate valid but likely low-yield because the source failure arose inside a large existing codebase with count-asserting tests while the derived task is greenfield with the anti-pattern named. Section 8 of the same document says the axis that works is whether the agent's natural self-check covers the rule; a fifteen-line pure function is small enough that most self-checks will.
predictions.falsifier: Two or more countable reward-0 trials, at least one from each provider family, whose blind labels agree on capability.

stoppingRules.rule: If all four first-stage trials are clean solves, stop and report VALID-BUT-EASY. Do not buy more slots.
If at least two countable reward-0 trials occur including one from each provider family, stop buying slots and proceed directly to blind labelling.
If exactly one reward-0 occurs, or reward-0 occurs in only one provider family, preregister and run at most four additional slots, two per provider.
Maximum campaign size is 8 clean trials. No ninth clean trial is bought under any outcome.
No benchmark solve-rate bound is claimed from this campaign. Clopper-Pearson intervals over the observed attempts are reported instead, and they are wide at this size.

spendCaps.estimateBasis: ESTIMATED, not measured. Derived from this repository's Phase 14 subject telemetry ($1.99 over 4 Anthropic attempts) and Phase 16 reader telemetry ($2.9878 over 4 Anthropic reads). OpenAI attempts are unpriced and add an unknown amount on top.

labellingPlan.freshness: Each labeller is a fresh container with no repository mount and no other label output.
labellingPlan.packet: evidence only: the visible challenge package, the submission, the verifier output and the transcript
labellingPlan.agreementRule: Difficulty evidence counts only when both labellers independently choose `capability`. Disagreement means unlabelled: not capability, and not specification failure.
secondaryDistinction: broad implementation failure unrelated to the intended mechanism
labellingPlan.noInheritance: A trial's label is never inherited from another trial merely because the two share a failed-check shape.
labellingPlan.writeOrder: Labels are written to disk before the campaign verdict is computed.

decisionRules.TRANSFER-READY: Probe V2 passed, package and reader gates passed, at least two agreed capability failures, at least one capability failure from each subject-provider family, failures concentrated on the intended identity-binding or associated selection checks, and no repeated specification, verifier, capture or infrastructure defect.
decisionRules.VALID-BUT-EASY: The package is valid and the maximum campaign produced no agreed capability failure.
decisionRules.INCONCLUSIVE: Evidence appears in only one provider family, labels disagree, or valid slots cannot be completed within the cap.
decisionRules.CANDIDATE-INVALID: The exact probe, contract, verifier, witness boundary or package controls failed.
